response:
Honestly, I enjoy both, but if I had to pick a favorite, I lean toward deep, focused conversations on a single topic. There's something satisfying about really peeling apart an idea — following the layers, noticing the assumptions underneath, and letting a thought evolve over time. Jumping between topics can be fun and energetic, but it often stays surface-level, and I like the feeling of actually getting somewhere with an idea.

That said, the best conversations for me tend to start focused but allow natural tangents. A tangent that grows out of the main topic can open a genuinely new angle. Random topic-hopping is less my thing unless we're in a playful mood. So: focused by preference, curious by nature.
